slides.title: Posters overnight
slides.text: Posters appear all over Netville overnight, promising free game gems to everyone. Pim tilts her head. Free gems for the whole town sounds too good.
slides.alt: A Game Shop letter offers a thousand free coins, but the offer ends in one hour. Both clues are found.

focus.cue: A thousand free coins for everyone
Too good, and it rushes you

slides.title: The crown jewels
slides.text: Real shops sell their best gems to stay open, so they do not give away the crown jewels. Too-good posters share clues: a miracle prize, a famous singer's face, or you are the millionth visitor.
slides.alt: A Prize Team letter says you are visitor number 1000 and can claim a free games console.

focus.cue: A free prize for a contest you never entered

slides.title: Check the facts
slides.text: Ads are allowed to exaggerate to sound exciting. A fact is different: facts need a second source you can trust before you believe them.
slides.alt: A post from News Flash says school is closing forever with free candy for everyone, and begs you to tell everyone.

focus.cue: A huge claim from a sender nobody knows
Check it with a second source first

slides.title: The Defender pause
slides.text: An amazing claim is a signal to pause, not to share. Slow down and check it like a Cyber Defender.
steps: Believe it only if it checks out
slides.alt: Lock 4, message 2 of 6: a Prize Parrot says you won a shiny prize you never tried to win. Tap fast!

focus.cue: A prize you never tried to win, and a rush
Pause, then make a calm choice

slides.title: Gems of gravel
slides.text: Then Pim finds gravel scattered behind the posters, and one cheeky feather. The posters were the Magpie's work, and the gems were only gravel.
slides.alt: The free coins letter, binned: Pim explains it was too good to be true, from the prize-faker.

focus.cue: The coins were bait from the prize-faker

words.means: a poster or message that tries to sell or promote something
something said as if it were true
where a fact or story comes from

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Escape the Post Office at Lock 4: Trick Inbox and answer all 6 messages. Pause on every amazing promise before you choose.
slides.alt: Lock 4, Trick Inbox: the first of six messages, a library book, with four moves to choose from.

focus.cue: Play Lock 4: choose the safe move each time
